day_shape: 78 items dominated by Khamenei funeral logistics — Tehran airspace closure Monday, heads of state from Iraq, Tajikistan, Armenia, Georgia, Turkey VP, Pakistan PM arriving — alongside UNSC emergency session on US-Iran clashes and Bahrain, IDF Gaza/Lebanon strikes, and Israel marking 1,000 days since October 7.

threads.label: Khamenei funeral: foreign delegations arrive
threads.summary: Regime channels reported the arrival in Tehran of the presidents of Iraq, Tajikistan, and Georgia, Turkey's Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz, Armenia's Prime Minister, Uzbekistan's parliament speaker, and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif for the funeral of Ali Khamenei. IRIB and Defa Press said Tehran airspace will be fully closed Monday and listed delegations from Russia, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Yemen, and Hezbollah/Nasrallah family members paying respects.

threads.label: UNSC emergency session on US–Iran, Bahrain
threads.summary: The Security Council met at Bahrain's request following resumed US–Iran military confrontation and Iranian attacks on Bahrain, with UN Assistant Secretary-General Elizabeth Spehar urging maximum restraint to preserve the 17 June US–Iran Memorandum of Understanding. US Ambassador Michael Waltz warned Trump's patience was "not unlimited"; the UK's James Kariuki expressed solidarity with Bahrain and Kuwait.

threads.label: IDF Gaza and Lebanon operations
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Muhammad Na'im Jandiya, identified as Hamas Shuja'iyya battalion security chief who abducted Cpt. Daniel Perez and held hostages Yotam Haim, Samar Talalka and Alon Shamriz; Defence Minister Katz said 83% of Hamas tunnels in IDF-held Gaza have been demolished. In southern Lebanon, a reservist was severely wounded in Bint Jbeil, a Hezbollah operative was killed at the Ali Taher ridge, and weapons caches were located at At-Tiri and Maroun al-Ras.

threads.label: 1,000 days since October 7
threads.summary: Israel marked 1,000 days since the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack with memorials, marches and protests in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. IDF chief Eyal Zamir and Defence Minister Katz issued a warning to Iran during the commemorations.

threads.label: Iranian military posture and threats
threads.summary: Joint Command chief Ali Abdollahi threatened a "harsh and regrettable response" if Israel or the US attack Iran during Khamenei's funeral, per Jerusalem Post; Iran International reported IRGC special forces deployed along the Persian Gulf coast to track ships using the Oman-side Hormuz route. CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper cited a C-UAS unit in Bahrain that shot down 14 Iranian one-way attack drones, and reporting said CENTCOM is considering relocating Gulf bases to Israel's Negev.

threads.label: Iran internal: arrests, coercion, Kurdish clashes
threads.summary: Iran International reported the re-arrest of environmental activists Houman Jokar and Sepideh Kashani from the 2018 espionage case, and complaints of pressure on workers, businesses and charities to attend Khamenei funeral events. Jerusalem Post reported Iranian strikes on Kurdish opposition groups following clashes with PJAK, while a former national volleyball coach was charged with 10 sexual offences in Canada.

IDF troops are continuing to scan the area for the gunman as of this morning.

events.title: Enabling Supersonic Overland Flight
events.summary: This proposal would advance the United States' leadership in next-generation aviation by replacing the longstanding prohibition on civil supersonic flight over land with a modern, performance-based regulatory framework. Consistent with national policy set forth by the Executive Order of June 6, 2025, Leading the World in Supersonic Flight, this action would enable the safe, efficient, and commercially viable operation of civil supersonic aircraft in the United States. Current regulations prohibit flight operations of civil aircraft at a true flight Mach number greater than 1 in the U.S., except under the conditions and limitations of an operation-specific authorization from the Administrator, to protect the public from sonic boom. FAA has determined the general ban on civil supersonic flight is outdated and no longer appropriate due to advancements in technology, flight techniques that prevent sonic booms from reaching the surface, and increased interest in civil supersonic flight. FAA proposes to repeal this outdated and unnecessary prohibition and establish a corresponding interim noise-based certification standard to allow supersonic flights without an operation-specific special authorization clearing the way for next-generation supersonic flight. This rule removes regulatory barriers, provides clear pathways for testing and early commercial operations, and positions the United States to serve as the leader in setting global standards for supersonic flight. These actions will ensure that the United States leads the world in the safe, lawful, and rapid development and deployment of next-generation supersonic aviation.
